meta.parties: Mahawithana v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue

rules.statement: An adventure in the nature of trade can be established where an individual secures an option to purchase land and sells portions of it for profit, without intending to hold the entire property as an investment.
rules.supporting_quote: In pursuance of the intention, which the Board rightly in my opinion attributed to him, he agreed to purchase 583 acres but in fact he ultimately purchased for himself on 31st December 1954 only 119 acres. The dictum of Viscount Dunedin cited above refers to the intention not to 'hold an investment', but the assessee here certainly made no 'investment' whatever covering the 400 odd acres which constituted the fields actually sold to others on 31st December 1954, or covered by firm sale agreements.
